page.layout: One printed page, single text column, no margin notes. Running head at top, page number at top right. Catchword "mihi" at the lower right of the column.

main_text.l: Abunde est, quo damna Reipublicæ si-
ne Ecclesiæ ruinâ resarciantur. Illius qui-
dem libenter Restaurator audiam, haud ta-
men eâ conditione, ut sub obtentu publici
æris liberandi, hujus merito dicar Oppressor.
Satis erat quæ contraxit causa improba, hoc
vero pacto dissolvere, multo foret deterius.
Deus faxit, ut nec Ego hec Mei funus un-
quam huic culpæ affines.
Ad te Domine preces meas dirigo, enixe obtestans
ut hanc subditis meis ignoscas temeritatem j-
urandi, & acriorem in illis postea sensum effi-
cias, quo illa justa, moralia, nullatenus remit-
tenda vincula à Verbo Tuo & Regni Legibus
conscientiis eorum imposita, accuratius in post-
erùm observent, à quibus multi Pietatis[?], aut
Reformationis respectus satis erunt illos obsol-
vendo, nedum in Partem adversam transfire per-
mittent.
Fac ut serò tandem cogitent, nil violentum
& injurium cum Religione constare.
Tu nullius Sacrilegium approbas, qui sic Ze-
lum suum offendit in detestando Idola.
Tu per Regum Sapientissimum docuisti, la-
queum esse homini Sanctum devorare, ac postea
ad vota converti.
Custodi Famulum Tuum usque, ne consentiat
in perjuras & sacrilegas rapinas, ne stigma

page.notes: Printed ornament marks (a small bullet before "Custodi" and a small mark before "Fac ut" and "Ad te") are printer's signs, not text, and are left out. The large initial "A" of "Ad" is set as a decorative letter and is read as "Ad". "Pietatis" is read as "Pictatis" in the scan and is marked [?]. The gap above "Ad te" and the gap above "Fac ut" are spacing only. The word "hec" is printed as shown. The running head is in Greek and Latin characters as printed; the final letter of the Greek word is read as Η.
